clue.text: Missed final? Nothing replaces Arsenal's crown

indicators.note: the letter for nothing takes the place of the named letter in the word for final

parts.note: final means last

indicators.note: a crown is the top, so the first letter of Arsenal's

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A football fan regrets missing a cup final, perhaps one Arsenal failed to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal's crown is its first letter, A; swap it in LAST for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something missed, like a chance or a ball, is said to be lost: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Business relationship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a matter or concern

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like a business partnership; the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a matter of concern and a romantic liaison, typically an illicit one.

clue.text: As a finish to hatter's ambition?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom meaning 'on top of everything else'
second meaning, read literally: a hat-maker would like to put a cap on everything

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for a final crowning touch, but read literally it is what a maker of caps dreams of.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces the last and worst (or best) item in a series, as a finishing flourish.

clue.text: King breaks nose, shirtless, of rugby player

indicators.note: the letter for King breaks into the shortened nose, sitting inside it
a T-shirt is a shirt, so shirtless means losing a T

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A rugby player with a broken nose, stripped to the waist, is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from HOOTER (a shirtless 'T-shirt') to give HOOER, then K breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the hooker is the front-row forward who hooks the ball back in the scrum.

clue.text: Novelist drops back knowing one's a pest

indicators.note: the novelist's name loses its back, that is its final letter

parts.note: Graham Greene, the English novelist
fly is British slang for knowing or sharp

explanation.surface: A novelist steps back, aware that he has become a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are aphids, small insects that damage garden plants, so they are a classic pest.

clue.text: Short reptile in half of China

indicators.note: take the first half of the word for china

parts.note: china, as in plates and cups, is crockery

explanation.surface: A small reptile is found in half of the country of China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is the tableware, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the informal shortening of crocodile, so it is a reptile in short form.

clue.text: Welsh football manager once hugged by Kitty as 'a man of the people'

indicators.note: the manager's name sits inside the word for kitty, held as in a hug

parts.note: a kitty is a pot of pooled money
Tony Pulis, the Welsh former manager of Stoke and others

explanation.surface: A former Welsh football boss is embraced by his pet cat as a popular figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty is a pool of money, not a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A populist claims to represent ordinary citizens against elites, so styles himself a man of the people.

clue.text: Long to decorate? Not I!

indicators.note: Not I tells us to leave the letter I out of the word for decorate

parts.note: to paint a room is to decorate it

explanation.surface: Someone asked to decorate refuses the job outright.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant for something is to yearn for it, so it is a verb synonym of long.

clue.text: Ground flour? Of course, no longer sure — it's faded

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
the letters of the following word are no longer included in the mix

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A baker notes the flour has been ground, but is no longer sure it is still fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix the letters of FLOUR OF COURSE, take out S, U, R and E, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-colour describes something that has lost its proper hue, so it looks pale or washed out.

clue.text: In the Mirror, comic Brand plugs impression of wine

indicators.note: a mirror image is reversed, so the result is read backwards
the comedian's name plugs the gap inside the word for impression

parts.note: an air is an impression or appearance someone gives
Jo Brand, the British stand-up comic

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper prints a comedian's impression of a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Mirror looks like the newspaper; here it signals reversal of AJOIR. Jo Brand is a British comedian, not Russell.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red (or white) wine from the Spanish region of that name.

clue.text: Sailor steals one advanced piece of jewellery

indicators.note: the sailor takes in the letter for one, holding it inside

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sailor pockets a valuable piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband, a kind of jewellery worn by royalty and brides.

clue.text: How to maintain an accurate tally of fortified towers?

definitions.text: How to maintain an accurate tally
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for tracking a number
second meaning, read literally: a keep is a castle's fortified tower, so a count of keeps

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the idiom; the second treats the first word as a noun, the central tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep count is to track a running total, exactly what an accurate tally requires.

clue.text: Brexit negotiator swaps note with Republican fence

indicators.note: one letter is exchanged for another in the negotiator's name

parts.note: Michel Barnier, the EU's chief Brexit negotiator

explanation.surface: The EU's Brexit negotiator trades places with an American Republican over a border fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a physical barrier that blocks passage, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Whisky calls?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... is a brand of Scotch whisky
second meaning: ... ring out as calls, as to church

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the Scotch brand name Bell's, written without its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell's is a blended Scotch brand, and bells are rung as calls or summonses.

clue.text: Elves are beautiful in elegant stripy tops

parts.note: fair means beautiful, as in a fair maiden

indicators.note: the tops of the three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Elves look lovely dressed in smart striped tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves and fairies are both small magical folk of folklore, close enough to be loose synonyms.

clue.text: Simultaneously elected soldier and three students taking English

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: the three letters take in the abbreviation for English

parts.note: L for learner, a student driver, three times

explanation.surface: An elected soldier and three students learn English at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done in parallel run side by side at once, the same idea as at the same time.

clue.text: A bit of her novel is set within Scotland's borders

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the border letters

parts.note: the borders of Scotland are its first and last letters, S and D

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of her are made new by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written; these three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passage of her novel is set in the Scottish Borders region.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book title's descriptor; here it means new, so the pronoun is reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a small scrap or bit, as in 'not a shred of evidence'.

clue.text: Material carried by wobbly crate

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the next words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Some fabric is being transported in a rickety crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a stretchy synthetic fabric, a trade name for spandex used in sportswear.

clue.text: Pisa can't be rebuilt by leaders

indicators.note: rebuilding something puts its parts together in a new order

explanation.surface: The leaning city of Pisa cannot be rebuilt by its leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Captains are the heads of teams or ships, so they are leaders in the general sense.

clue.text: Time for an old political journalist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a unit of time
second meaning: Sir Robin ..., the British broadcaster famous for grilling politicians

explanation.walkthrough: Robin Day was a combative BBC political interviewer of the late twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A day is a period of time, and Robin Day was a celebrated political interviewer.

clue.text: Discontented Japanese leave teas, wanting Eastern favourites

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter for Eastern goes
the letters of the emptied Japanese leave the teas

parts.note: Darjeelings are teas from the Indian hill district

indicators.note: with its contents gone only the outer letters of Japanese remain

explanation.surface: Unhappy Japanese visitors leave their teas, preferring Eastern favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: Discontented Japanese is J and E; take those from DARJEELINGS to get DARELINGS, then lose the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlings are much-loved people, the ones someone favours, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Lord installs square safe

indicators.note: the lord installs the letter inside himself

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, a lord
a T-square is a draughtsman's tool, so T for square

explanation.surface: A nobleman has a square safe fitted in his home.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old criminal slang for a safe, as in a peterman (safecracker).
explanation.definitionFit: In underworld slang a peter is a safe or strongbox; safe-crackers were petermen.

clue.text: More flexible to take Latin during meal

indicators.note: the letter for Latin comes during the meal, placed inside it

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more flexible by studying Latin over dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means bending easily, so its comparative describes something with more flexibility.

clue.text: Penny's annoyed by design originally being copied without permission

parts.note: P is short for penny
irate means angry or annoyed

indicators.note: the origin of design is its first letter

explanation.surface: Penny is cross because her design has been ripped off.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirated material, such as films or software, is copied illegally and sold without the owner's consent.

clue.text: Soldiers go back-to-back during exercise, 1 out of 10?

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters come during the exercise, placed inside it

parts.note: PE is physical exercise at school
GI is an American soldier; two of them back to back, the first turned round, give IG and GI

explanation.surface: Soldiers perform back-to-back drills in training; one in ten scores badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a toe: the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy' counts the ten toes as piggies.
explanation.definitionFit: In the toe-counting rhyme each toe is a little piggy, so one piggie is one of ten toes.

clue.text: Naughty child can regularly keep reading

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of keep

parts.note: reading is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: A mischievous child can be relied upon to keep on reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker is a British word for a mischievous youngster, as in 'you little tinker'.

clue.text: Bishop walking and picking fruit

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rambling is walking for pleasure in the countryside

explanation.surface: A bishop goes for a country walk and gathers fruit on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Brambling is gathering blackberries, the fruit of the bramble bush.

clue.text: Blackbird's dish?

parts.note: read as black plus bird: B, the pencil-grade abbreviation for black, and an owl, a bird, make up the vessel

explanation.walkthrough: Split blackbird into black and bird: B for black (as on pencils) and OWL for the bird, giving a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a round, deep vessel for serving food, which is what a dish is.

clue.text: Young people cry when lifted up over your head

indicators.note: the reversed cry is laid over the next letter, enclosing it like a cover
in a down answer, lifted up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: the head of your is its first letter

explanation.surface: Children cry when a parent swings them up over their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys are young males, so the answer names young people of one sex.

clue.text: National enters 25 countries

indicators.note: the letter for national enters the cross-referenced word

parts.note: 25 is BOYS, which can also be lads

explanation.surface: A national team enters the competition with twenty-five countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25-down, BOYS; use its synonym LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lands are nations or territories, a common synonym for countries.

clue.text: Walk dogs, perhaps in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: dogs are an example of pets

explanation.surface: Someone walks the dogs now that they have retired.
explanation.definitionFit: To step is to walk with a pace, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Woman returns recent delivery with contents missing

indicators.note: the word for recent goes back, read backwards

parts.note: new means recent

indicators.note: losing its contents leaves only the outer letters of delivery

explanation.surface: A woman sends back a recent parcel because it arrived empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Wendy is a female given name, so it names a woman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Queen always follows a half of stout with tablet

indicators.note: the word for always follows the half of the stout
take the first half of the stout's name

parts.note: Guinness is the famous Irish stout
ever means always
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A queen always follows a half-pint of stout with a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: A half of stout sounds like a pub measure; here it means half the letters of GUINNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinevere was the legendary wife of King Arthur, queen of Camelot.
